annotations.title: Add or update a form on a site

description: Declares a built-in form on a site you own: its fields (text, email, textarea, checkbox, month, date, tel, select), the recipient email (kept on the server, never in the page), the button label and the thank-you message. Entries are saved and emailed from Pagetool, behind Turnstile, a honeypot, a minimum fill time, rate limits and field validation. Returns form_key and placeholder_html: put placeholder_html in the page HTML where the form should appear (replace_page_html, or stage then publish_staged). Pass form_key to update an existing form. For any date or month question use a month/date field here (past dates are never offered, and recurring events via occurs drop off once they pass) rather than a raw <input type="date"> in page HTML, which the server cannot check. Free.

classes.description: Optional Tailwind/CSS class strings to style the form to match the page.

form_key.description: Omit to create a new form; pass an existing form_key (from a previous call) to update that form.

name.description: The form's name, used in the notification subject "<Site name>: new <name>", e.g. "Open mic sign-up". 1-120 characters.

recipient_email.description: Where entries are emailed. Stored on the server only; never appears in the page.

site_key.description: The site the form belongs to. Must be yours.

stage.description: true = stage this form change with the page: visitors keep the live form until publish_staged (discard_staged drops it); preview at staged_preview_url. The operator token always stages on a published site. Omit for an immediately live change.

success_message.description: Shown after a successful entry. Default "Thanks! Your entry was sent." Max 300. May include {field_name} for a text, select, email or tel field, e.g. "Thanks, {name}!"

name: upsert_site_form
